### Summary

`EquilibriumOptions` lists the components, the phase of each, the reactions as equation strings, which phase is the
ideal gas, and four numerical options. It can be built field by field through the API or read from a YAML file whose
`phases`, `species`[^rg-065f0144b433] and `reactions` blocks give the same information. The YAML reader also checks that every reaction
conserves every element. The API path cannot, because it carries no compositions. Building `EquilibriumTP` from the
options forms the stoichiometric matrix and refuses linearly dependent reactions.

::: {.callout-note title="At a glance"}
**Purpose.** Define the system of @eq-ch05-conditions-residual and the options of @sec-ch05-newton.

**Data.** Components, phases, phase of each component, reaction equations; four numerical options.

**Placement.** Before the first solve; `EquilibriumTP` reads the options when it is built.

**Activation.** `EquilibriumOptions.from_yaml(path)` or the API setters.

**Guarantee / limits.** Element balance is checked only by the YAML reader; at most 64 components.

**Evidence.** See the Tests layer below.
:::

Symbols as in @sec-ch05-conditions.

### Derivation

No derivation: this scheme maps an input to the matrices $\mathsf S$ and $\mathsf E$ and the phase map $\pi(n)$ of
@sec-ch05-conditions.

### Numerical method

`EquilibriumOptionsImpl::from_yaml`
({{< code src/equilibrium/equilibrium_options.cpp EquilibriumOptionsImpl::from_yaml >}}) reads the file in order:

1. **Phases.** Each entry of `phases` has a name and a list of species, which become the components in the order
   listed. The phase whose `thermo` (or `type`[^rg-9292dca86f77]) is `ideal-gas` is the gas phase. Exactly one phase must be, and a
   component may belong to only one phase. Any other `thermo` value makes a condensed ideal mixture.
2. **Species.** Each entry of `species` has a name and a `composition`[^rg-54a1072b5f2c] map. Every component must have one, and a
   species defined twice is refused. The elements are the union of the composition keys.
3. **Reactions.** Each entry of `reactions` with no `type`, or with `type: equilibrium`, is kept; every other type is
   skipped, so a file can also hold the kinetics of @sec-ch06. Every kept reaction must name only components and must
   balance every element to $10^{-10}$; otherwise the reader raises "does not conserve element".
4. **Numerical options.** An optional `equilibrium` block sets the four values below.
5. **Validation.** The options must have non-empty lists, one phase index per component and in range, at most 64
   components, a gas phase in range, positive standard pressure, `max-iter` and `ftol`, and a non-negative
   `mole-floor`.

The checks of step 5 are in `EquilibriumOptionsImpl::validate`
({{< code src/equilibrium/equilibrium.cpp EquilibriumOptionsImpl::validate >}}).

| key | meaning | default | read by |
|---|---|---|---|
| `standard-pressure` | $p^\circ$ of @eq-ch05-conditions-activity [Pa] | $10^5$ | `from_yaml` |
| `max-iter` | Newton iterations, also the inner bound of the least-squares fallback | 50 | `from_yaml` |
| `ftol` | relative tolerance of @eq-ch05-diagnostics-error | $10^{-8}$ | `from_yaml` |
| `mole-floor` | lower bound on every amount [mol] | $10^{-30}$ | `from_yaml` |

: Keys of the `equilibrium` block. {#tbl-ch05-options-keys}

The same defaults apply when the block is absent or the options are built through the API
(`EquilibriumOptionsImpl`, {{< code src/equilibrium/equilibrium.hpp EquilibriumOptionsImpl >}}). Building
`EquilibriumTP` runs `EquilibriumTPImpl::reset`
({{< code src/equilibrium/equilibrium.cpp EquilibriumTPImpl::reset >}}), which validates again, forms the
stoichiometric matrix from the equation strings in component order, and refuses it unless its rank equals the number
of reactions. A reaction that is a combination of others would make the Jacobian of @sec-ch05-newton singular.
@fig-ch05-options-path follows a YAML file to the solver.

```{python}
#| label: fig-ch05-options-path
#| fig-cap: "From a YAML input to the buffers of EquilibriumTP. Boxes in reading order; grey notes give the checks made at each stage."
#| fig-alt: "Five boxes left to right: phases, species, reactions, validate, EquilibriumTP; notes under them: one ideal-gas phase, each reaction balanced in every element, at most 64 components, reactions independent."
#| echo: false
from kintera_report.ch05.figures.fig_options_path import make_fig
make_fig()
```

The kintera example `examples/equilibrium_nasa9.yaml` is such a file: one `ideal-gas` phase with H$_2$, O$_2$ and
H$_2$O, the reaction H$_2$ + ½ O$_2$ $\rightleftharpoons$ H$_2$O, and an `equilibrium` block with `max-iter: 100`. The runs of this chapter
use small inputs of the same form written by `run_equilibrium.py`. The two-phase ones give a second phase with
`thermo: ideal-solution` or `thermo: pure`; any value other than `ideal-gas` gives a condensed ideal mixture.

### Tests

| test (ctest name) | what it asserts | tolerance | where the tolerance comes from |
|---|---|---|---|
| `test_equilibrium.release`, YAML case | components, phase ids, only the `equilibrium` reaction kept, `standard-pressure` and `max-iter` read, stoichiometry signs | exact | parsed values |
| `test_equilibrium.release`, unbalanced case | A $\rightleftharpoons$ B with A = H and B = H$_2$ is refused | exception | the reader's check |
| `test_equilibrium.py` (`test_python_core_binding_is_functional`) | options built through the Python API solve a reaction | `atol=1e-7` | not stated in the test |

: Tests of the options. {#tbl-ch05-options-tests}

The two `test_equilibrium.release` rows are the gtest cases `EquilibriumOptions.ReadsSpeciesAndReactionsFromYaml`
and `EquilibriumOptions.RejectsUnbalancedYamlReaction`. Both pass on both builds (@sec-ch05-conditions, Tests). No test covers the one-gas-phase
rule, a component in two phases, the 64-component limit or the rank check.

### Limits

- **The API path does not check element balance.** Options built with the setters carry no compositions, so an
  unbalanced reaction is accepted and the solve conserves whatever the equation strings conserve.
- **At most 64 components**, a limit of the active-set solver used as the fallback.
- **One gas phase.** A file with no `ideal-gas` phase, or with two, is refused.

<!-- reader glossary notes -->
[^rg-065f0144b433]: species — list of species maps; required; its order fixes the species index; read by `init_species_from_yaml`; [source](https://github.com/chengcli/kintera/blob/0d9f67f97d841147e23283d2dcdab302238d2c45/src/species.cpp#L148-L155)

[^rg-9292dca86f77]: type — name of the rate form; each reader keeps the entries of its own type; required; compared with the reader `name()`; [source](https://github.com/chengcli/kintera/blob/0d9f67f97d841147e23283d2dcdab302238d2c45/src/kinetics/arrhenius.cpp#L58-L62)

[^rg-54a1072b5f2c]: composition — map from element symbol to count; the molar mass is computed from it; passed to `molar_mass`; [source](https://github.com/chengcli/kintera/blob/0d9f67f97d841147e23283d2dcdab302238d2c45/src/species.cpp#L165-L170)
